title: Settings and instructions: the policy helper's claudeMd tier
status: implementation, verification and one bounded independent review with its repairs
sourceBehaviour: lr() returns the helper state output unless it was armed from remote; M2n() returns that output's claudeMd or null.
qZn pushes the helper block as {path:EEo,type:"Managed",content:bn} only when the text is truthy, between the managed directory's own file and the settings document's claudeMd.

zt() fingerprints policySettings.claudeMd, M2n(), claudeMdExcludes, autoMemoryEnabled, env and ir(); Jt re-evaluates it and on a change calls gk(e) and Cx(e,"policy_refresh"), clearing the cached userContext so the next prompt is rebuilt.
The static default fallback output is {managedSettings:...} only, so the default tier supplies no instruction text.
hostAdaptations: managedHelperSchema is the strict managed-policy schema plus claudeMd; the CLI validates the helper document with it. policyHelper.defaultPolicy keeps the plain managed schema because the settle only takes text from a served document.
loadProjectConfig and loadChildInstructions insert policyHelperText under <policyHelper> after the managed directory's files and before the settings document's claudeMd.
refreshPolicyHelperInstructions rewrites the once-built prompt section in place, keeps memory blocks, and journals policyHelperText; the CLI settle calls it after every helper refresh.
Only the helper tier supplies text (serving === 'helper'); the static default payload's claudeMd is not used.

applyManagedPolicy rebuilds the policySettings permission layer from the applied policy in the slot the loaded layer occupies (or before cliArg when the document first declares one), removes the layer when the document declares no layer field, and the settle re-seeds the live permission owner with reloadPermissionState; this repaired a defect that left the startup managed policy in force (the W08 driver's served case was red at the W369 commit).

validation.redBaseline: compiled CLI before the change: {claudeMd:...} was refused with 'policy does not match the managed policy schema' and the request lacked the text; the served case was also denied because the stale policySettings layer stayed in force

defectsRepaired: applyManagedPolicy replaced the managed base fields but kept the previous policySettings permission layer, and the live permission owner kept the rules seeded at open, so a helper document's policy never replaced the startup managed policy. The layer is now rebuilt from the applied policy and the settle re-seeds the owner with reloadPermissionState.

Review finding 1: the rebuilt layer was appended last, so after startup it sat behind the cliArg layer and the CLI's reload capture (layers.at(-1)) recorded the managed layer instead of the CLI's, losing --allow-tool/--deny-tool on /reload. The layer now keeps its slot, or is inserted before cliArg when the document first declares one.

Review finding 2: the layer was rebuilt only when the new document carried permissions, so a document that dropped the block left the previous layer in force. The layer is now removed when the document declares no layer field, and an autoMode-only document still owns a rule-free layer.
Review finding 3: policyHelper.defaultPolicy accepted claudeMd while the settle ignores a fallback's text; the fallback now uses managedPolicySchema and refuses it.
Minor: an unused skillsSection import is removed, and SessionConfig['managedPolicy'] is the schema's inferred type so autoMode and useAutoModeDuringPlan are representable.
knownLimitations: A config without instructionSources cannot distinguish a memory block from instruction text; the live CLI, reload and every child build set the list.
The static default payload's own claudeMd is not used for instructions, matching the recovered default output.
The helper text is refreshed only through the CLI settle, reload and child builds; a host embedding that mutates config.system directly bypasses it.

Review finding 4: replaceInstructionSection finds the previous block span by 'Instructions from <path>:' headers, so a previous instruction file whose own text contains such a header line can move the cut inside the old section and re-append its tail. The function predates this package and serves every instruction refresh; the recovered product rebuilds its user context instead of cutting a span, so this is an edge case of the host's in-place rewrite.

Review finding 5: the CLI settle wiring is covered by the compiled driver rather than a unit test, the project's convention for CLI wiring; the journaled helper tier's reload is now asserted in test/reload.test.ts.
